topics.label: Introduction to complement and lecture framing
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the opening framing, contextualizing complement within immunology and introducing the lecture.

topics.label: Complement system principles, nomenclature, and C3 activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational concepts of the complement cascade, including its general organization, naming conventions, and the central cleavage mechanism of C3.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three distinct recognition pathways—alternative, lectin, and classical—that drive convertase formation and deposit complement on pathogen surfaces to reach the activation threshold.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of activated complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the downstream effector outcomes of complement activation: opsonization, inflammatory signaling, and direct cell lysis via the membrane attack complex.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory proteins and mechanisms that protect host cells from accidental complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Clinical manifestations of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the distinct clinical presentations and disease vulnerabilities resulting from genetic and secondary deficiencies across different complement components.

topics.label: Mechanisms of pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details how pathogens, exemplified by Staphylococcus aureus, have evolved mechanisms to resist and inhibit complement activity.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and preview of adaptive immunity
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the closing remarks and previews the upcoming lecture on the adaptive immune system.
